newsitem.title: USA: Pakistan wants IMF/World Bank back on its side.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan wants IMF/World Bank back on its side.

text.p: Pakistan is working to get back into the good graces of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank, an adviser to Prime Minister Benazhir Bhutto told the international lending agencies on Wednesday.

"We are determined to restore the relationship to one of full cooperation and trust and reaffirm our commitment to stabilisation and reform," Bhutto's financial adviser V.A. Jafarey told then annual IMF/World Bank meeting.
The IMF withheld an $80 million tranche due in June, and part of a $600 million standyby loan, pending a review of Pakistan's 1996-97 budget.
Bhutto is currently in New York where later this week she is due to hold talks with Stanley Fisher, number two at the IMF, on a suspended lending programme.

Jafarey, due to fly to New York to join Bhutto, said Pakistan had continued to pursue its agenda of adjustment and reform and that economic growth had improved while inflation was showing signs of easing.
"We recently implemented a tough budget which ran into fierce opposition at home and triggered an intense media campaign of exageration and disinformation," Jafarey said.
The IMF halted a $1.5 billion Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility last year because the government had missed agreed targets to cut the budget deficit and reform tarrifs.
The World Bank has also criticised Pakistan for not reducing its debt fast enough. It also expressed concern over the size of Pakistan's military spending.
